The normalized-cut cost of 0.532 is relatively high, which per metric semantics reflects more cross-boundary connectivity and weaker graph support for preserving the boundary, and must not be read as evidence for preserving distinct units. The union spectral structure peaks at k=2 (leading eigengap 0.487 versus 0.422 at k=1), indicating a possible two-way internal subdivision of the union; per scope interpretation this supports preserving the current boundary only when that subdivision is also meaningfully aligned with the current two-way structure, and here the ARI of 0.846 indicates substantial alignment. This is triage-level structural observation on the candidate-generation consensus geometry; it does not establish biological meaning or clinical validity and does not recommend accept, drop, split, or merge.
